name: vin on 5v
twin_lines: bme280_1 = bme280 (conf 0.88): VIN@B40, GND@B41, SCL@B42, SDA@B43
net_1: bme280_1.GND <-> esp32_1.GND | holes A14,A41,B41,C14,RAIL_TOP_MINUS | via w_black_1 (conf 0.90), w_black_2 (conf 0.90)
net_2: bme280_1.SCL <-> esp32_1.GPIO22 | holes A42,B42,I18,J18 | via w_green_1 (conf 0.84)
net_3: bme280_1.SDA <-> esp32_1.GPIO21 | holes A43,B43,I15,J15 | via w_yellow_1 (conf 0.86)
net_4: bme280_1.VIN <-> esp32_1.5V | holes A19,A40,B40,C19,RAIL_BOTTOM_PLUS | via w_red_2 (conf 0.90), w_red_3 (conf 0.90)
net_5: esp32_1.3V3 | holes A1,C1,RAIL_TOP_PLUS | via w_red_1 (conf 0.90)
question: Is it safe to power this on?

findings.title: VIN is on 5V, max is 3.6 V
findings.explanation: bme280_1 VIN is powered from esp32_1 5V (5 V). The bme280 datasheet limits the supply to 3.6 V, so this can damage it.
findings.fix: Move the red wire from RAIL_BOTTOM_PLUS to RAIL_TOP_PLUS
